builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Fused-Softmax for efficient quantized attention
summary: The method replaces the standard vector-unit softmax inside attention with a reformulated, approximated softmax whose dominant operations are folded into the attention GEMMs, shifting work to matrix cores. It costs an implementation tied to AMD CDNA 4 hardware (MI355X) via the AITER library, requires MXFP8/6/4 quantization of attention operands, and adds approximation error that the authors claim stays below the GEMM quantization error floor. It can fail on non-AMD hardware where no kernel exists, and accuracy may degrade on workloads whose quantization error floor is lower than the video-generation model validated in the paper.
rationale: The speedup is substantial and training-free, but the kernels ship only for AMD MI355X-class hardware, so a reader with a single 24 GB GPU or API-based inference cannot deploy them and should monitor for ports to other architectures.
technique: Fused-softmax quantized attention on matrix cores

claims.statement: The method replaces the standard vector-unit softmax inside attention with a reformulated, approximated softmax whose dominant operations are folded into the attention GEMMs, shifting work to matrix cores. It costs an implementation tied to AMD CDNA 4 hardware (MI355X) via the AITER library, requires MXFP8/6/4 quantization of attention operands, and adds approximation error that the authors claim stays below the GEMM quantization error floor. It can fail on non-AMD hardware where no kernel exists, and accuracy may degrade on workloads whose quantization error floor is lower than the video-generation model validated in the paper.

MXFP8/6/4 kernels reach roughly 3.0/4.0/4.6 PFLOP/s on MI355X (2.1x/2.8x/3.2x over BF16 attention); a hybrid MXFP6/4 schedule gives up to 2.05x end-to-end speedup on Wan2.2-T2V-A14B with preserved visual quality.
